name: Water pollution
d24Text: Water pollution. Usually related with excessive concentrations of organic matter, nutrients suspended solids, but also heavy metals, plastics, pharmaceuticals, among other pollutants.

name: Connectivity barriers
d24Text: Connectivity barriers. A total or partial alteration in the longitudinal connectivity of a lotic ecosystem (e.g., by culverts, weirs, grids, bridges, dams).

name: Altered hydrological properties
d24Text: Altered hydrological properties (e.g., increased runoff and flashiness, reduced baseflow, rapid flow variability).

name: Geomorphological changes of the channel
d24Text: Geomorphological changes of the channel. For example, by channel incision or widening, bank erosion and instability, sediment imbalance, loss of natural channel complexity.

name: Artificialization of the channel and banks
d24Text: Artificialization of the channel and banks. Using artificial materials in the riverbed (e.g., concrete, culverts, non-local materials – sand, stones, boulders, and metal grids) and banks (e.g., concrete, gabion and laid stones) leads to poor transversal connectivity, groundwater dysconnectivity and drives the ecosystem to a sterile state.

name: Occupation of the floodplain
d24Text: Occupation of the floodplain. Constricts the natural available space for the riparian area, natural floods and infiltration (e.g., constructed areas such as buildings, roads or sidewalks - impervious areas; private gardens, vegetable garden – non impervious areas).

name: Removal or degradation of the riparian vegetation
d24Text: Removal or degradation of the riparian vegetation (total or partial removal, alteration in the structure and species composition expected at the site; presence or invasion by exotic plant species; fragmentation of habitats and riparian corridors).

name: Lack of expected aquatic habitats
d24Text: Lack of expected aquatic habitats. Loss of pools, riffles, and woody debris; deposits of inorganic and organic matter, macrophytes disappearance).

name: Altered physico-chemical properties
d24Text: Altered physico-chemical properties (e.g., low dissolved oxygen, high water temperature, acidification).

name: Degraded biological communities
d24Text: Degraded biological communities (e.g., presence of invasive aquatic animals and plants, and altered food webs; Haubrock et al., 2022).

name: Catchment pressures
d24Text: Catchment pressures. (e.g., high impervious surface cover, intense urban land use, groundwater extraction).
